text:
sana: Hey, observed persistent VRAM growth on A100 when running long-context chat (40k+ tokens). eviction counters increment but free memory stays low. not sure if pager is failing to reclaim or pages are leaking into a ghost list. attaching minimal logs below. :thinking:

sana: log snippet:
```
[2026-03-18T14:03:12Z] pager: evict 412 pages -> queued for reclaim
[2026-03-18T14:03:12Z] pager: reclaim attempt 1 -> freed 0 pages (rc=-22)
[2026-03-18T14:03:12Z] kvcache: resident 12.8GB -> 18.1GB (after longctx)
[2026-03-18T14:03:12Z] mm: free-list length 0
```

sana: repro: a100 (driver 470.x), batch_size=1, seq_len=40k, tiled-paged-attn enabled, quant=fp16. H100 seems fine in same infra.

ev an: can you paste the exact run command / config? trying to reproduce locally.

sana: sure, minimal runner:
```
./run_infer --model redwood/7b --device a100:0 --pager tiled --batch 1 --max-tokens 40000 --kernel-select auto
```

evan: got it, will try. initial thought: could be kernel selection differences between hw. jon, any profiler traces?

jon: ran a quick perf and saw kernel mismatch at page reclaim paths. on H100 we pick `pager.compact-v3` kernel; on A100 we consistently pick `pager.streamed-v1` (fallback). here's the trace snippet: 
```
[krnl] pager_select_kernel() -> pager.streamed-v1 (score 42)
[krnl] pager_reclaim_start -> launching 512 threads
[cuda] cudaMemcpyAsync -> returns ok
[krnl] reclaim_done -> freed_count=0, leaked_markers=3
```

jon: also saw repeated PT (page table) walk logs with `owner_id` alternating between 0 and -1 right before reclaim returns 0. suspicious race on owner tagging.

pri: @sana @jon fwiw, earlier we had a bug where streamed-v1 assumed PCIe ordering for frees; on some A100 driver combos DMA ordering differs and stale entries can remain visible. forcing `pager.use_compact=true` (select compact-v3) fixed reclaim for my repro but increased tail p50->p95 by ~30ms.

pri: quick workaround to test: add env `RW_PAGER_FORCE=compact-v3` or set `kernel-select=compact-v3` in config and repro.

maria: ran the forced-compact experiment on A100 and H100 across same job id. results:
- A100: growth stops, resident stabilizes ~12.9GB. tail latency +32ms.
- H100: no change (already stable).

maria: infra-bot kicked off perf job: run_id=infra-20260318-0921, nvml traces attached to job.

infra-bot: perf job infra-20260318-0921 started on a100-pool-7. logs: https://ci.internal/runs/infra-20260318-0921 :robot_face:

evan: thanks. so root hypothesis: streamed reclaim kernel has a race with PT freelist metadata under PCIe ordering on certain A100 drivers. possible remedies: (1) tighten memory ordering in streamed-v1 kernel, (2) prefer compact-v3 for workloads with longctxs, (3) add a reclamation sanity pass that re-walks freelist when freed_count==0.

jon: added low-noise instrumentation patch to print owner_id state transitions. will open PR with trace flags: PR#4521.

pri: couple of notes — compact-v3 uses a different work distribution and reduces freelist contention but does more global reductions (hence latency hit). streamed-v1 was optimized for p99 on short ctxs.

maria: recommend short-term: expose config knob to prefer `pager=compact` for customers using long-context LLMs and add metric `pager.reclaim_zero_count` to detect regressions. medium-term: fix streamed-v1 ordering + tests.

sana: assigning owner to threads/tasks: @jon will land instrumentation and a repro test. @pri will prototype ordering fix in kernel and measure. @evan to run perf job matrix across driver versions (470.x, 510.x). i'll own the customer outreach and temporary config toggle.

evan: quick question — do we have a reproducer that uses MI250/AMD? want to know if this is NV-link/PCIe specific or generic.

jon: tried on mi250 (rocm 6.5) — reclaim succeeds but with different perf characteristics. doesn't reproduce the leak. points back to NV/A100 driver ordering quirk.

pri: actionable next steps:
- add `pager.reclaim_zero_count` metric + alert (sana)
- PR for streamed-v1 ordering guard (pri)
- add e2e repro job in CI that runs 40k token run on a small gold dataset (evan)
- customer toggle `pager.force=compact` (sana + infra)

maria: jotting down timeline: quick toggle deploy today, instrumentation PR this week, kernel patch prototype next week, rollout after perf validation.

sana: thanks all. adding snippet for the sanity re-walk if reclaim returns zero (cheap and safe):
```
if (freed_count == 0) {
  msync(); // fence host-visible ordering
  rewalk_freelist();
}
```

jon: lgtm as temp. will comment on PR with trace output when ready.

pri: also add a unit stress harness that toggles kernel selection randomly to catch this earlier.

sana: cool. closing loop once infra run finishes. :white_check_mark:
